description.value: A functional MRI study of Korean proverb processing, comparing figurative proverbs with literal sentences and opaque with transparent proverbs while controlling familiarity.

quotes: This study investigated the processing area of the Korean proverb in comparison with the literal sentence using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Furthermore, we hypothesized that proverb processing may be affected by the transparency/opacity of the language also in fMRI experiments, with a specific focus on the interpretation of proverbs in Korean when familiarity is set to the same level.

description.value: Within-subject task study in which 15 healthy Korean-speaking adults silently read opaque proverbs, transparent proverbs, and literal sentences during fMRI. Stimuli were presented pseudo-randomly in blocks.

quotes: For each participant, a total of 36 proverbs and 18 literal sentences were presented pseudo-randomly in one of three predesigned sequences (Figure 1).
All sentences were presented on a screen while the participant was lying inside the MRI scanner.
The task was to read the sentences, and the feedback was verbally reported after the fMRI scan.

description.value: Participants silently read Korean opaque proverbs, transparent proverbs, and literal sentences presented visually while lying in the MRI scanner.

quotes: All sentences were presented on a screen while the participant was lying inside the MRI scanner.

description.value: Opaque Korean proverbs whose metaphorical interpretation was difficult to derive from the evoked image.

quotes: Some types of proverbs are highly transparent, whereas others are nontransparent; thus, the metaphorical interpretation is difficult to make without knowing the figurative language.

description.value: Transparent Korean proverbs whose meaning could be elicited from the evoked image.

quotes: The term transparency describes whether or not a meaning can be elicited from the evoked image (Glucksberg et al., 1993).
